brief.goal: Trace local, static local and global variables to predict each labelled line.
rules: Each function has separate local and static local variables, even when names match.
Automatic locals are initialized on each call; static locals retain values between calls.
Each helper is called once; global and main-local updates occur before the calls.
Use values at the moment of printing and preserve all eight labelled lines.

concept: Scope determines where a variable's name refers to its storage. Ordinary local variables belong to individual function calls, while a static local keeps its value between calls and a global exists for the program's lifetime. Identical local names in different functions still identify separate variables.

explanations.text: This header supplies declarations: information C needs to use the standard input and output functions.
This variable is global because it is declared outside all functions. It exists throughout execution and is available to later functions here.
This helper returns no value. Its local variables belong to this function even when another function uses the same names.
An ordinary local is created and initialised for each call. This one is separate from every other variable named local.
A static local is initialised once and retains later changes between calls. Its name is still usable only within this function's block.
Display this helper's two current values before updating them. Each %d formats an integer; each \n ends a labelled line.

Execution starts here. The braces group the steps belonging to the program's starting function.
